title: Raw feedback clusters and impact hypotheses (Mar 2027)
content:
Purpose: quick, minimally-processed cluster dump from 18 customer interviews, 42 support threads, and three field-engagement sessions (Feb–Mar 2027). This is NOT polished — intended for product + eng to scan and pick hypotheses to validate.

Notes on method: manual affinity clustering by theme, counted frequency tags (approx), added a rough impact hypothesis and estimated engineering lift (S/M/L). Representative verbatim quotes where useful. Links to raw threads in linked_artifacts.

High-level signal summary (one-liner): customers want predictable, lower-cost token usage across variable prompts, clearer failure-mode observability for routing/fallbacks, and faster on-ramp for dedicated/private rollouts with less infra coordination. Secondary: better debugging tools for embeddings and reranking.

Clusters (raw) — rank by frequency marker (F: high/med/low):

1) "Token-explosion" unpredictability (F: high)
- Problem: unexpectedly large token counts from certain system+user prompt mixes (templated prompts with long examples). Drives cost spikes and billing surprises.
- Representative quote: "We did a monthly run and our bill jumped 3x because of a few noisy templates — we had no guardrails." — mid-market analytics team
- Impact hypothesis: a per-request token guard + proactive alerting would reduce bill surprises and lower churn for cost-sensitive customers.
- Estimated lift: M
- Possible MVP: server-side soft-limit warnings (70/90/100% thresholds) + per-template token preview in Console.
- Open Qs: Should warnings be adaptive (based on historical per-route distribution)? Tie to quotas or only alerts? See JIRA-CS-4123.

2) Fallback confusion / opaque routing behavior (F: high)
- Problem: when a model is unavailable or autoscale fails, fallback to variants occurs but customers report silence or different output quality; hard to trace what happened.
- Quote: "We saw a different tone and no indicator that fallback kicked in — our app went weird for a day." — AI-native startup
- Impact hypothesis: exposing explicit route/fallback decisions (headers + Console timeline) reduces incident MTTR and product regressions by ~50%.
- Lift: M
- Suggested components: per-request routing trace (reason, chosen model variant, latency tier), Console view for route trace, correlate with rollouts.
- Notes: product and SRE already have prototype tracing hooks — link to ENG spike (JIRA-ENG-6891).

3) Embedding drift and mismatch (F: med)
- Problem: customers see search relevance degrade after model updates or quantization changes; unclear how to compare embedding spaces.
- Quote: "After we switched to the new quantized model our semantic search stopped finding older docs." — legal tech customer
- Impact hypothesis: a compact embedding regression harness + per-deployment similarity-stability metric would cut regressions and increase confidence for auto-updates.
- Lift: L-M (requires eval infra and dataset storage)
- MVP: a small 'stability score' computed on a fixed benchmark prompt set surfaced in Console and in model catalog.

4) Dedicated onboarding friction (F: med)
- Problem: dedicated/private setup requires too much cross-team coordination (networking, KMS, infra naming) — stalls pilots.
- Quote: "We spent 3 weeks aligning IP ranges and our infra team still had questions." — enterprise customer
- Impact: reducing time-to-first-query for Dedicated from weeks to days likely increases conversion rate on enterprise POCs.
- Lift: M-L (multiple teams: infra, security, product)
- Quick wins: improved onboarding checklist, templated Terraform + sample KMS config, and a 'preflight' validator that flags common network misconfigs.

5) Cost/latency transparency per token (F: med)
- Problem: lack of token-level cost breakdowns by route/model and limited visibility into per-token latency contributors (KV cache hits, batch wait time).
- Quote: "We need to know where, exactly, we're paying more — is it batch wait or the model?" — e‑comm platform
- Hypothesis: exposing token-level cost + latency waterfall reduces blame-game across infra and product and supports better config choices.
- Lift: M (backend and Console additions)
- MVP: token-level breakdown for top 5 slowest routes over last 24h, exportable CSV.

6) Prompt-versioning and canary visibility (F: low-med)
- Problem: canarying prompt/template changes is manual; no built-in diffing/rollout metrics for prompt experiments.
- Quote: "We want to iterate prompts like feature flags — roll out to 10% and measure."
- Impact: prompt canaries reduce regressions and allow safer improvements to prompt engineering across teams.
- Lift: M (requires metric hooks + per-route sampling)
- MVP: simple 10/90 split with automatic metric collection (latency, token count, quality via sampling).

7) Reranking tooling gaps (F: low)
- Problem: customers building reranking pipelines lack small, easy-to-run eval harnesses and sample configs; current docs too abstract.
- Quote: "We rewrote our reranker three times before it felt right — wish we had a template."
- Impact: plug-and-play reranking templates + scoring scripts reduce time-to-production for search/recommendation teams.
- Lift: S-M (mostly docs + examples)
- MVP: two example reranker configs (vector+LLM score) and a reproducible notebook.

Cross-cutting quick wins (can be actioned in 1–2 sprints):
- Per-route token preview modal in Console (ties to cluster #1).
- Preflight checklist + Terraform snippets for Dedicated onboarding (#4).
- Two practical reranker examples and a short walkthrough video (#7).

Prioritization buckets (very rough):
- Immediate (Q2 scope): Token guards & alerts; routing trace; per-route token preview; reranker examples.
- Near-term (Q3): Token/latency breakdown exports; prompt canary MVP.
- Backlog (Q4+): Embedding stability suite; full Dedicated preflight automation.

Unresolved questions / decisions needed:
- Tying token soft-limits to billing quotas vs notifications-only (product + finance tradeoff).
- Data retention/PII considerations for storing prompt templates for preview (security). Need security sign-off.
- How much of routing trace detail do we surface without exposing internal infra identifiers? SRE input needed.

Action items (owners assigned where clear):
- Product: draft proposal for per-request token guard UX and policy options (owner: Linda Park) — due 2027-03-22.
- Eng: spike to expose routing trace in headers and Console stub (owner: Rafael Ortiz) — spike results by 2027-03-19.
- CS: schedule 3 follow-ups with top-5 affected customers to validate guard/warning designs (owner: Maya Chen) — complete by 2027-03-25.
- Docs: assemble two reranker example repos and a 10-minute walkthrough (owner: Amina Shah) — draft by 2027-03-30.

Notes to self / raw scraps:
- Many customers conflate "fallback" with "rate limiting" — may need clearer terminology in docs.
- Consider defaulting to conservative soft-limits for newly created routes (opt-out). Risk: surprise for advanced users.
- Match CS flags to customer tiers: enterprise customers prefer opt-in stricter policies.

If you care about validation prioritization: pick 2 hypotheses to validate with small experiments next sprint: token-guard alerts (quick product mock + CS user test) and routing trace header (eng spike + internal rollout to dev team).

Raw references (some shared in linked_artifacts but repeating for convenience):
- Confluence: Feedback Archive Q1-2027 (see collection of raw transcripts).
- JIRA: CS-4123 (token spikes), ENG-6891 (routing trace spike).
- GH: PR 789 (console token preview prototype).

— end of dump —

Status: lightweight, intentionally messy. Use as input to a prioritized discovery plan rather than as a public artifact.
